description: We are a multidisciplinary team of university students passionate about technology, AI, data, space, and product development. Our team combines project management, AI/ML, data analysis, frontend development, UX/storytelling, and space-health research to build practical solutions for real-world space challenges.
summary:
‏AstroSentinel – Astronaut Health Monitoring System

‏We propose to develop AstroSentinel, a smart astronaut health monitoring system designed to track astronauts' physical condition during space missions.

‏The system will collect health information through wearable sensors and regular manual health assessments, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, body temperature, sleep duration, and stress levels.

‏At the beginning of the mission, the system will establish a personal health baseline for each astronaut. New measurements will then be compared with this baseline and predefined medical safety ranges to identify unusual changes and potential health risks.

‏When abnormal readings are detected, AstroSentinel will generate alerts that explain the detected issue and recommend appropriate preventive actions, such as resting, repeating a measurement, or contacting the medical team.

‏All collected information will be displayed through an interactive dashboard, providing health indicators, historical charts, organ-specific monitoring, and risk notifications.

‏The system will combine automated data analysis, rule-based monitoring, and optional AI assistance to support early detection and help astronauts maintain their health throughout space missions.
details:
AstroSentinel – Astronaut Health Monitoring System

NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

AstroSentinel is an innovative astronaut health monitoring system designed to support crew safety and well-being during long-duration space missions. Spaceflight exposes astronauts to unique health challenges, including microgravity, space radiation, sleep disruption, and physiological changes that require continuous monitoring and rapid response.

Our solution combines an interactive 12-organ Digital Twin with a health-monitoring dashboard to provide a clearer view of an astronaut’s physical condition. The system tracks key health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep duration, and stress levels. It also provides organ-specific monitoring interfaces and visualizes health trends over time.

AstroSentinel uses a rule-based analysis system to classify health readings into three levels: Normal, Warning, and Critical. When an abnormal reading is detected, the system activates a smart dual-channel voice protocol: Channel 1 provides routine health reports, while Channel 2 interrupts normal reporting to announce important warnings and recommended actions. This hands-free communication approach is particularly valuable in microgravity environments, where astronauts may have limited ability to interact with screens while performing medical procedures.

The platform also includes interactive visual scanning simulations, organ-specific telemetry, health charts, and a mission-oriented interface. Its architecture is designed for future integration with wearable biosensors and portable ultrasound devices, allowing real-time health data collection.

What makes AstroSentinel distinctive is its combination of anatomical visualization, continuous health monitoring, rule-based anomaly detection, and voice-guided alerts in one unified platform. Rather than relying entirely on artificial intelligence, the initial system uses transparent, predefined medical monitoring rules, with the possibility of adding AI-assisted analysis in future versions.

Our long-term vision is to develop AstroSentinel into a reliable health-support platform that helps astronauts recognize potential health risks earlier, supports medical decision-making, and contributes to safer human exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

AstroSentinel – Monitoring Health, Protecting Life, and Supporting Humanity’s Journey Beyond Earth.
